synopsis: The corpus consistently dates application of EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 to 20 January 2027, before the prototype and mid-2027 validation campaign; the glossary says it applies directly across EU member states [f52, f6696, f10700, f15062]. Annex I Part A covers self-evolving machine-learning safety components and machinery embedding them, with notified-body involvement on every conformity route, but whether a trained-then-frozen detector falls within that scope remains disputed and unsettled [f2090, f363, f2091, f7435]. Software ensuring safety functions is described as a safety component, while other chapters identify protection against corruption and, through a secondary summary, recording of safety decisions and software versions [f9789, f5833, f5649]. Simulation acceptance remains uncertain: no relevant acceptance guidance or outside assessor was identified, no simulation-credibility acceptance criteria are defined by the cited regulation and standards, and published notified-body lead times were not found despite a warning that they could exceed the four-month validation window [f8184, f8185, f8242, f5110, f259, f11928]. The harmonised-standards list was still being prepared in 2026 and no standards had yet been cited; machinery AI requirements are reported to come through delegated acts, with an unverified commentary discussing an interim role for AI Act standards until acts expected by 2 August 2028 [f2092, f10501, f2096, f7431]. Planning should therefore include primary-source verification: several chapters explicitly did not verify regulatory dates or implications, Chapter 12 relied on secondary summaries rather than the Official Journal, and the synthesis recommends re-checking regulatory dates after October 2026 [f4335, f5111, f2012, f9463, f55].
